chapter_title: Concerning the Man who is ugly in his Body, [but]
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
:
 The Formation
 of
 Pear
ls in
 the Sea


**
¶9.
** Precious interior truths do
 not arise in every region of the natural
 mind,
 nor are
 they formed throughout the whole of worldly
 thought. Rather, in certain particular states
 within the natural mind, interior truths
 are formed.
 In
 those
 states
 of
 the natural mind where
 interior
 truths can
 take
 shape
, the self-love native
 to that
 mind blazes upward and descends
, and
 it produces preliminary appearances of truth —
 as
 when
 a discrete influx of divine truth flows
 down from
 heaven into
 the natural degree
, desc
ending as truth from the celest
ial realm
 into
 pur
ified natural truths.


**¶10.** This
 discrete influx of divine truth descends
 to the purified natural truths,
 and they absorb it and are united
 with it. It does not sink into
 the deepest obscurities of the
 natural mind, but remains
 upon the surface of conscious thought. The
 preliminary appearance and the containing form are shaped
 around
 this wholesome influx,
 and it becomes a precious interior truth.
 When
 the influx of heavenly truth enters
 the natural mind
 without
 remaining
 whole, it breaks and separates into
 many partial truths, and it requires
 time to become a purified natural truth
.
 It rises within the natural mind from the
 union of heavenly truth and natural
 truth,
 and it is received into the containing form
, which at first is merely a preliminary
 appearance. They are joined with
 each other at
 this stage
, and are shaped and become a great
 interior
 truth —
 a noble and precious
 kind
.

**¶11.**
 When, however, a single influx
 of heavenly truth falls and that
 infl
ux breaks into many partial truths and
 various fragments of
 truth, they are formed into and confined
 within numerous lesser interior truths, each
 within its own containing form. One form
 may hold two truths, another may
 hold three, others may hold five;
 some contain
 more than
 these, some fewer.

**
¶12.** Now
, when a whole and undivided
 influx of divine truth is found
, and the containing form receives it entire
, it becomes a great and precious interior
 truth whose
 worth is perfected. However
, if two partial truths have time
 to adhere to one another before any
 fragment escapes, and they unite with
 each other, and the containing form receives
 them before they divide
 further — they too are
 shaped into a great and valued spiritual good
.

**¶13.**
 Behold, this
 teaches how interior truths are formed within
 the natural mind. As a precious truth
 comes into existence by means of heavenly
 truth that has time to develop into a
 preliminary appearance, so
 the
 containing form comes into existence from that appearance
, and the appearance itself ar
ises through the transformation and
 working
 of the natural mind.

**
¶14.** Then
 immediately,
 at
 the time when those
 who seek interior truths disc
ern where they are formed, they desc
end to those states and bring precious tru
ths up from the depths of the natural
 mind, and each seeker finds according
 to the providence that
 is ordained for him. The seekers
 deliver them to the intermediary beings,
 and the intermediary beings deliver them to
 the highest celestial states and
 the powers
 of heav
enly life.

**¶16
.** The goods
 rescued from captivity are like the infl
ux of heavenly truth,
 while the apostles are like those who
 retrieve
 interior truths from the depths.
 The intermediary beings are the angels who
 transmit the
 light
 of heaven; the highest
 celestial states and
 the powers of heavenly life are the
 eternal
 orders
 of divine
 wisdom.

**¶17.
** For
 all the souls that rise
 up
 out
 of the embodied life of mankind and
 are freed from the natural degree shall
 be restored to the great celestial states
 of wisdom and
 love
. A state of eternal
 peace comes
 about for them,
 there
 in
 the
 highest orders
 of heavenly life.

---


*Note on
 
¶9
:
 The "
fire
 of
 the sea" that
 produces
 "
foam" presents
 a striking correspondence
 —
 the self
-love (
fire) inher
ent in the natural mind,
 when
 acted
 upon by desc
ending divine
 truth (
rain
), produces the
 first
 rough
 external
 appearances (
foam) from
 which containing
 forms (
shells
) can
 develop
. This is the
 necessary
 prec
ondition:
 without the
 ag
itation of the
 natural mind by
 infl
owing
 truth
, no
 vessel
 exists
 to
 receive and crystall
ize an
 interior truth. The sea
 does
 not produce the
 pearl
 from
 itself
; it
 produces only
 the shell
.
 The pearl is
 formed solely
 from what
 desc
ends from above
.*

Rather, in various places that are in this sea, pearls are formed in them [ ... ... ] that sea, in which the [pearls] shall be formed [ ... ] this [ ... ... ] what the sea shall [ ... ... ] its fire {blazes} above and comes [down ... ... ] and it makes foam like the drop of water that flows [ ... ] down in rainwater [ ... ] is the water [ ... ... d]own first [ ... ... ] foam and comes down [ ... ... ] the sweet waters [ ... ... ] the waters.

“This drop of water shall [ ... ] down to the sweet waters and [ ... ] and they absorbed them and were combined with the [ ... ]. They did not [d]escend to the depths of the sea, but they [ ... ... ] it floated on the surface of the waters [ ... ... ] to it. The foam and the pearl-shell shall be formed [ ... ] this wholesome drop [ ... ... ] it, and it becomes a pe[arl ... ] that makes a drop of rainwater [ ... ] waters [ ... ] it not being whole. It breaks and separates out into many droplets, and it has time to become a drop of sweet water [ ... ] and comes up in the sea of [ ... ] rain and sweet water; and it is accomodated in the shell, which at first is foam. They shall be joined with each other at [this] time, and are shaped and become a great pea[r]l, a great and valued kind.

“Now, when you might [find a] whole drop, and the shell receives it, it shall become a great and valued [pe]arl as its worth is perfected. [However], if these two droplets will have time (to adhere) to one another before any (water particle} escapes, and they mix with e[ach o]ther, and the shell [ ... ] before they break into [ ... ] within [ ... ] in a great kind [ ... ... ] the drop of rain, which [ ... ... ] another one, that [ ... ... ] the [w]aters form them in [ ... and] in a great, valued commodity.

“Behold, [I, I have] taught you how sea-pearls shall be formed. I have told you that as a pearl shall come into existence by means of rainwater that has [ti]me to become foam, the pearl-shell shall come into existence by means of the foam, and the foam itself comes into being by means of the transformation and the [ ... ] of the sea.

“Then immediately at the time when [ ... ... ] the pearl divers know it, they shall [ ... ] and they [ ... d]own to those places and they bring pearls up from the depths of the sea, and each pearl diver finds according to the fortune that is [ordai]ned for him. The pearl divers shall [gi]ve them to the traders, and the traders give them to the kings and the nobles.

“[The] booty that shall be seized is like the dr[op of r]ainwater, while the apostles are like the divers. The traders are the light-givers of the heavens; the kings and no[b]les are the aeons of greatness.

“Fo[r a]ll the souls that ascend in the flesh of mankind and are freed shall be brought back to the great aeons of light. A place of rest comes about for them, at that place in the aeons of greatness.
